question: Should OpenClaw add one generic adaptive inbound debounce contract, keep fixed debounce as the supported core behavior, or defer smarter timing to a channel/plugin seam first?
rationale: The request adds public config and changes how inbound fragments become agent turns, so automation cannot safely choose increment/max defaults, count-trigger behavior, typing-signal trust, transcript shape, or per-channel rollout policy.

options.title: Design one opt-in adaptive contract
options.body: Add a single generic inbound debounce policy with explicit initial/increment/max or equivalent semantics, plus schema, docs, and tests across core debounce and representative channels.

options.title: Keep fixed debounce only
options.body: Document messages.inbound.debounceMs/byChannel and queue modes as the supported batching answer, then close smarter timing requests as not planned.

options.title: Require a plugin/channel seam first
options.body: Defer core config until a typed channel or plugin ingress hook can provide provider-specific typing/count signals without growing global message config.

recommendation.title: Design one opt-in adaptive contract
recommendation.body: Add a single generic inbound debounce policy with explicit initial/increment/max or equivalent semantics, plus schema, docs, and tests across core debounce and representative channels.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across shared inbound debounce policy, ordering fixes, and product-review context for this area.
